newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares finished stronger on Thursday, propelled higher by positive sentiment from Wall Street and other world market's recent rallies, dealers said.

They said Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals' comments this week that interest rates could be cut before the end of the year also continued to fuel local and offshore buying interest on the industrials.

"Basically world markets were very firm overnight, the FTSE and the Dow were up...and I think this interest rate cut talk is still around in our market," one dealer at the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said.

Reiterating his Wednesday's remarks, Stals told Reuters on Thursday he believed that recent inflation and money supply data was encouraging and could pave the way for a rate cut before the end of the year.
But he added that it was impossible to be precise about when conditions would be right to cut the key Bank rate from its current 17 percent level.

Among shares which rode high on offshore interest were chemicals group Sentrachem when an offshore buyer took 667,000 shares in a deal worth around 5.2 million rand by stockbrokers Barnard Jacobs Mellet.
The stock ended up six cents at 796 cents with volumes at 5.6 million rand.

The industrial index finished up 28.1 points at 9,150.5 -- a new life high, with golds taking no cue from industrials' jovial mood as bullion continued to struggle to break through the $328 an ounce resistance level.
The gold index dropped 1.2 points to 981.4, while the all-shares climbed 10.8 points to 7,484.5.

Dealers said Thursday's currency weakness, which saw the rand weaken to a six month low of 4.61, had been largely ignored as the currency had already been discounted to soften to around 4.65 by the end of the year.
"Our market doesn't seem perturbed by the rand's weakness," one dealer said.
One of the day's biggest gainers was information technology firm Q Data which jumped 150 cents to close at 11.40 rand.
Dealers said interest in the stock had been rekindled by news that it had signed a three million rand deal to supply hardware and software to medical aid firm Interdoc.
Overall market volumes were high with 80.3 million shares worth around 985 million rand changing hands in a market expected to remain buoyant on Friday.
"All the eyes are now on the international markets now that the local economic indicators are out of the way. I see a firmer market tommorrow (Friday)," a dealer said.

Despite bullion woes, individual shares on the gold board managed to edge higher, as Vaal Reef ended up 225 cents at 238.25 rand, Kloof up 20 cents at 24.00 rand, while Eastvaal dropped 10 cents to close at 480 cents.
Dealers said near-dated share futures which firmed up early on Thursday had came off slightly in the afternoon amid Wall Street's shaky start.
The September industrials contract was last at 8,685/95 from 8,667 settlement, golds contract at 695/700 from 702 settlement, and the all-shares contract at 6,705/23 from 6,724 settlement.
